=== ONE NON-BLOCKING FINDING, RECORDED NOT CHARGED ===

tests/core/test_lwb_proof_required.py::test_no_shipped_policy_file_arms_this_rule_to_deny now carries a rationale this very PR falsifies. Its docstring says deny "fails open when facts are missing (a bare repo, no `.git`, a corrupt or detached HEAD all permit)" and its assertion message says "Deny fails open when repo facts are missing, so it is advisory, not a control ... Make deny fail closed before shipping a policy that turns it on." After this change, deny does NOT fail open for `repo is None` or `facts_incomplete` -- and the sentence that reads as the guard's unlock condition ("make deny fail closed") is precisely what this PR just did. The guard itself should STAY (the PR's own docs correctly keep deny out of "security control" status because the detached-HEAD-no-PR-number bypass and the parser under-match list remain open), but the next contributor who trips this assertion will read a message that is no longer true and names a precondition already met.
Why I do not fail the PR on it: it is prose in a test message, it makes no check vacuous, the test still enforces exactly what it enforced before, and no gate covers it (lwb_check_state_claims passes -- it scans tracked docs for volatile git/PR state, not test rationales). Recorded so it is not lost; blocking a correct, well-scoped, well-tested fix over a comment string is the kind of veto that gets a gate routed around.

`config.mode is RuleMode.DENY` uses identity comparison on a `(str, Enum)`. I drafted this as a fragility finding -- RuleConfig(mode="deny") built by hand would silently fail OPEN -- then checked reachability: `is` is the house idiom (engine.py lines 69, 97, 100 all use it), and config.py's loader always builds RuleConfig via RuleMode.coerce (line 120), so a bare string cannot reach a rule through load_policy. Pre-existing repo-wide convention, not this PR's doing, and not reachable in production. Not a finding. (The 016Yb3Nh record reached the same conclusion independently; I re-derived it rather than inheriting it.)
